techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries run commands and scripts through PowerShell, often with encoded commands, download cradles (IEX/DownloadString), hidden windows or execution-policy bypass flags.
techniques.detection: Alert on powershell with -enc/-EncodedCommand, -nop/-w hidden, IEX or Net.WebClient in the command line, and on Office/browser/script-host parents spawning powershell. Review script block logs.

techniques.name: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: cmd.exe is used to chain commands, run batch files and launch other tools, frequently as the child of a document reader or web server.
techniques.detection: Flag cmd.exe spawned by winword/excel/acrobat/w3wp, long chained commands with & or &&, and cmd /c invoking certutil, bitsadmin or curl.

techniques.name: Unix Shell
techniques.description: bash/sh execute attacker commands, including reverse shells, one-line download-and-run pipelines (curl | sh) and commands launched from web-application processes.
techniques.detection: Alert on /dev/tcp redirections, curl|wget piped into sh, shells whose parent is a web server or database, and interactive shells with no TTY.

techniques.name: Python
techniques.description: Python interpreters run attacker code inline (-c) or from dropped scripts, used for reverse shells, loaders and data staging.
techniques.detection: Flag python -c with socket/subprocess/base64 imports, python started by web servers or cron from temp directories.

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.description: A victim opens a lure document, archive, shortcut or installer that starts the attacker's payload.
techniques.detection: Correlate a newly downloaded or mailed file with a process start from its path within minutes; watch double extensions and .lnk/.iso/.img content.

techniques.name: Phishing: Attachment
techniques.description: Email carries a weaponised attachment such as a macro-enabled document, script or archive that leads to code execution.
techniques.detection: Office applications spawning script hosts or shells, macro documents writing executables to user-writable paths.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Scheduled tasks created through schtasks or the task scheduler API run payloads at logon or on a timer to persist or execute remotely.
techniques.detection: Alert on schtasks /create with /ru SYSTEM, tasks pointing at temp or AppData paths, and tasks launched by non-admin tooling.

techniques.name: Cron
techniques.description: Crontab entries or files in /etc/cron.* run attacker programs repeatedly, often every minute from /tmp or /dev/shm.
techniques.detection: Monitor writes to crontab spools and /etc/cron.d; flag entries that fetch remote content or run from world-writable directories.

techniques.name: Windows Service
techniques.description: New or modified services launch malware at boot with high privilege; sc.exe and registry edits under Services are common.
techniques.detection: Alert on service creation whose binary path is in a user-writable directory or contains cmd/powershell, and on service installs by non-installer parents.

techniques.name: Systemd Service
techniques.description: Malicious unit files in /etc/systemd/system or ~/.config/systemd/user keep a payload running across reboots.
techniques.detection: Watch creation of unit files, ExecStart pointing to /tmp or hidden paths, and daemon-reload followed by enable.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Programs placed in Run/RunOnce keys or the Startup folder execute every time a user logs on.
techniques.detection: Alert on writes to Run/RunOnce, Winlogon and Startup folder by non-installer processes, especially values pointing at scripts or temp paths.

techniques.name: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
techniques.description: Commands appended to .bashrc, .profile or /etc/profile.d scripts execute whenever a shell starts.
techniques.detection: File-integrity monitoring on shell startup files; alert on additions containing curl, nc, base64 or reverse-shell syntax.

techniques.name: SSH Authorized Keys
techniques.description: Attackers append their public key to authorized_keys to retain passwordless access.
techniques.detection: Alert on modification of authorized_keys by processes other than the user's own ssh tooling or configuration management.

techniques.name: Create Local Account
techniques.description: A new local user, often added to administrators or sudoers, provides a durable backdoor.
techniques.detection: Alert on net user /add, useradd, new entries in sudoers or the Administrators group outside change windows.

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.description: Code is run inside another live process through remote memory writes, thread creation or ptrace to hide and inherit its privileges.
techniques.detection: Flag cross-process memory writes plus remote thread creation, ptrace attach to unrelated processes, and unbacked executable memory regions.

techniques.name: Process Hollowing
techniques.description: A legitimate process is started suspended, its image unmapped and replaced with malicious code.
techniques.detection: Suspended child creation followed by memory unmap/write and resume; image path that does not match in-memory content.

techniques.name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name
techniques.description: Malware copies the name of a trusted system binary (svchost, kworker, sshd) but runs from an unusual path.
techniques.detection: Compare process name with expected path and signer; alert on svchost outside System32 or kernel-thread names with a file-backed executable.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Payloads are packed, encoded or encrypted to evade static signatures, producing high-entropy files and long encoded strings.
techniques.detection: High section entropy, packer sections, long base64 blobs in command lines, scripts built from char-code concatenation.

techniques.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
techniques.description: Utilities such as certutil, base64 or openssl are used to decode staged payloads on the host.
techniques.detection: certutil -decode/-urlcache, base64 -d piped to a shell, openssl enc -d writing executables.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
techniques.description: rundll32.exe loads attacker DLLs or script content so the action appears to come from a signed Windows binary.
techniques.detection: rundll32 with javascript:, URL or temp-path DLL arguments, or without arguments, and unusual parents.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
techniques.description: mshta.exe runs HTA or inline script content, often fetched from a remote URL.
techniques.detection: mshta with http(s) or vbscript:/javascript: arguments; mshta launched by Office or email clients.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Regsvr32
techniques.description: regsvr32 with /i and a remote scriptlet executes code without writing a conventional executable.
techniques.detection: regsvr32 /s /n /u /i:http..., scrobj.dll loads, network connections made by regsvr32.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Security tooling is stopped, excluded or reconfigured to avoid detection, for example Set-MpPreference exclusions or stopping auditd.
techniques.detection: Alert on Defender exclusion changes, service stop of security agents, auditctl -e 0, tampering with agent files.

techniques.name: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.description: Event logs are cleared to remove traces of intrusion using wevtutil or PowerShell.
techniques.detection: Event 1102/104, wevtutil cl, Clear-EventLog by non-admin tooling.

techniques.name: Clear Command History
techniques.description: Shell history is deleted, truncated or disabled so executed commands are not recorded.
techniques.detection: history -c, unset HISTFILE, symlinking .bash_history to /dev/null, deleting ConsoleHost_history.txt.

techniques.name: Bypass User Account Control
techniques.description: Auto-elevating binaries and registry hijacks are abused to obtain a high-integrity process without a prompt.
techniques.detection: fodhelper/eventvwr/computerdefaults starting unexpected children, writes to ms-settings shell open command keys.

techniques.name: Sudo and Sudo Caching
techniques.description: Misconfigured sudo rules or cached credentials let attackers run commands as root.
techniques.detection: sudoers edits adding NOPASSWD, sudo invoked by service accounts, shells spawned via sudo from unusual parents.

techniques.name: DLL Search Order Hijacking
techniques.description: A malicious DLL placed where a trusted application searches first is loaded in place of the genuine library.
techniques.detection: Unsigned DLL loaded from the application directory that normally resolves from System32; new DLLs beside signed executables.

techniques.name: Dynamic Linker Hijacking
techniques.description: LD_PRELOAD or /etc/ld.so.preload loads a rogue shared object into every process, enabling rootkits and credential theft.
techniques.detection: Alert on creation or edits of /etc/ld.so.preload, LD_PRELOAD in process environments of system services, unexpected .so files in temp.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: The memory of lsass.exe is read or dumped to harvest credentials, using comsvcs MiniDump, procdump or custom tools.
techniques.detection: Non-system process opening lsass with VM_READ, rundll32 comsvcs.dll MiniDump, dump files of lsass written to disk.

techniques.name: /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow
techniques.description: Password databases are read and copied for offline cracking.
techniques.detection: Reads of /etc/shadow by non-privileged tooling, shadow copied to temp, unshadow or john/hashcat on the host.

techniques.name: Credentials In Files
techniques.description: Attackers search file systems for plaintext keys, tokens and passwords in configs, history and scripts.
techniques.detection: Mass grep or findstr for password/secret/id_rsa, bulk reads of .ssh, .aws, browser profile and config directories.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Repeated authentication attempts guess or spray passwords against SSH, RDP, SMB or web logins.
techniques.detection: Many failures from one source followed by a success, failures across many accounts with one password.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Operating system, hardware and patch information is gathered to choose next steps.
techniques.detection: Bursts of systeminfo, uname -a, hostnamectl, wmic os from a non-interactive parent.

techniques.name: Process Discovery
techniques.description: Running processes are enumerated to find security tools or targets.
techniques.detection: tasklist, ps aux or Get-Process sequences following initial execution, particularly when filtering for AV product names.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.description: Directories are listed and searched to locate documents, credentials or backups.
techniques.detection: Recursive dir /s, find / -name patterns across home and share paths launched by script hosts.

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
techniques.description: WMI is used locally or remotely to run processes, query systems and persist through event subscriptions.
techniques.detection: wmic process call create, WmiPrvSE spawning shells, new permanent event consumers.

techniques.name: Service Execution
techniques.description: Remote or local services are created to run commands, the pattern used by PsExec-style tooling.
techniques.detection: Short-lived services with random names, service binary in ADMIN$, cmd /c in service ImagePath.

techniques.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.description: Valid accounts are used over RDP to move between hosts and operate interactively.
techniques.detection: RDP logons from workstations that never act as jump hosts, tscon session hijack, enabling fDenyTSConnections changes.

techniques.name: SSH
techniques.description: SSH sessions with stolen keys or passwords provide lateral movement and tunnelling.
techniques.detection: New outbound SSH from servers, key use from unusual accounts, ssh -R/-D tunnels.

techniques.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Files are copied and executed through C$, ADMIN$ and IPC$ shares using valid credentials.
techniques.detection: Writes to admin shares followed by remote service or task creation; net use to many hosts in short time.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Tools and payloads are pulled onto the host with curl, wget, certutil, bitsadmin or script downloads.
techniques.detection: Download utilities fetching executables from raw IPs or newly seen domains and writing to temp, followed by execution.

techniques.name: BITS Jobs
techniques.description: Background Intelligent Transfer Service jobs download or run payloads and survive reboots.
techniques.detection: bitsadmin /transfer or Start-BitsTransfer to external URLs, jobs with notify command lines.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web
techniques.description: Malware blends C2 into HTTP(S) traffic using beacons with regular intervals and odd user agents.
techniques.detection: Periodic fixed-size requests, rare domains or IPs, scripts and unsigned binaries making web requests.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS
techniques.description: DNS queries carry commands or exfiltrated data through long encoded subdomains and TXT lookups.
techniques.detection: High-volume queries to one domain, long high-entropy labels, TXT-heavy traffic from non-resolver processes.

techniques.name: Encrypted Channel
techniques.description: C2 traffic is wrapped in custom or standard encryption to defeat content inspection.
techniques.detection: Self-signed or rare certificates, TLS on non-standard ports, unusual JA3 for the process.

techniques.name: Remote Access Software
techniques.description: Legitimate remote-control tools are installed or portable-run to provide interactive access.
techniques.detection: Unapproved AnyDesk/TeamViewer-like binaries, silent installs by scripts, new relay connections.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data
techniques.description: Data is compressed or encrypted before staging, with tar, zip, 7z or rar.
techniques.detection: Large archives created in temp from document directories, archive tools launched by script hosts, password-protected archive flags.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Collected data is sent back through the existing command-and-control channel.
techniques.detection: Outbound byte volume far above baseline to the beaconing destination shortly after archive creation.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
techniques.description: Cloud storage, paste or messaging web services are used as an exfiltration endpoint.
techniques.detection: Uploads to file-sharing domains by non-browser processes, rclone or curl -T/-F with large bodies.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Ransomware encrypts user files and appends new extensions, then drops a ransom note.
techniques.detection: Rapid modification or rename of many files with extension change, high-entropy writes, ransom-note creation in many directories.

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.description: Backups, shadow copies and recovery settings are destroyed to prevent restoration.
techniques.detection: vssadmin delete shadows, wmic shadowcopy delete, bcdedit recoveryenabled no, wbadmin delete, removal of snapshots and backup directories.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.description: Databases, backup and security services are stopped so their files can be encrypted or destroyed.
techniques.detection: Bulk net stop/systemctl stop of database, backup and endpoint-protection services.
